Rajiv / team —

Thanks — I’ve drafted a partner onboarding checklist and a lightweight certification matrix that covers pgvector hot-path behavior, S3 cold spillover constraints, auth (service-account vs. per-customer credentials), and support escalation tiers. Key clarifications for the buyer we need:

- Auth: We recommend customer-managed KMS + short-lived service tokens for routing to pgvector hosts. For the pilot we can accept managed keys but final will require KMS.
- Consistency window: Cold tier writes will be committed to S3 within 60s; search fallthrough logic favors pgvector when indices are warm. We document retry/backoff behaviour in the checklist.
- SLAs: Pilot: no SLA but target p99 within 450ms for hot-index queries; for production we can discuss Dedicated capacity.

Attaching partner-risk-matrix.xlsx (internal). Also looping Laura for the legal checklist — Laura, please flag any immediate no-gos in the MSA side.

Proposed triage: Thu 2027-07-22 11:00 PT — Ben, can you bring the integration checklist and a short diagram?

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi Laura / Priyom —

Attached are our redlines against your standard partner MSA. The high-level asks are: indemnity carveouts for data processed in cold tier (S3), a shorter retention window for embeddings (30 days default), and clarity around incident notification timelines (24 hours).

We can also sign an addendum limiting Redwood’s liability for third-party vendor outages (pgvector-hosts). If you have a negotiation playbook that accelerates these items (template clauses you prefer), please share.

Doc link: https://documentcloud.example/d/VectorOps-MSA-redlines

Thanks — we’d like to have an initial legal sync next week.
